races.name: Thomas Armstrong Group Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Apprentice Training Race - Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist with solid soft-going record who won over 12f at Goodwood last time; drops back in class here and Mark Loughnane has had a quiet 14 days, but the step up to 1m6f on soft looks a positive and Hope Regan's 5lb claim adds value — naturally suited to hunting from behind, which is less straightforward in this pace structure.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back and returning on a going and distance combination he has already encountered, Dream Harder looks primed on 28 days' rest and catches the eye with a speed rating of 80 backing his overall profile, though the fourth last time out keeps expectations measured.

runners_data.name: Yellow Card
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with strong recent form over extreme distances, winning over 22f and placed over 20f at Goodwood, but those efforts came on good ground and soft-going record over a shorter 15f trip shows no wins and no places; Isobelle Chalmers's 3lb claim helps but the going and trip combination is untested at this level.
runners_data.comment: Yellow Card has run over today's trip and going, and his rating edges above his official mark, making him a live each-way threat from a workable weight of 141 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, and that 56-day absence will need to be overcome on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: Carries a visor and recent form shows a spell of placed efforts including second over 14f at Goodwood; K.R. Burke's yard has been in decent form (7/43 over 14 days) and soft going is not a concern, but this horse's true racing style is at the rear of the field — pushed into a mapped midfield berth because the hold-up slots are full, which means it faces an awkward positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Gentle Warrior arrives here fresh after 34 days off, has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating puts him narrowly top of this field — though his recent record leaves him yet to win, and he will need to convert that promise at the weights carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-racing six-year-old with three placings in five runs including seconds over 14f and a third over 14f on good ground; has only one run on soft going in the last 15 trips and David Loughnane has a quiet yard at present, yet the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Cascade Hall closely on this course and distance.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without threatening at the top, Dance Time brings solid each-way form — third last time out and second two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, though she remains winless in recent starts and her 139 lb burden is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Expressionless
runners_data.note: Headgear (p) noted and recent form is modest — three fives, an eight, and a three in last six starts; Dylan Cunha's yard has been active (4/22) and the horse has soft-going experience over this general trip range, but its natural running style is from the rear, and being mapped to midfield due to crowding at the back means it is unlikely to produce its best work in this race configuration.
runners_data.comment: Expressionless shaped with promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while his rating of 74 puts him ahead of several rivals on these terms — the risk is that he remains winless in his last six starts and must prove he can convert that promise.

runners_data.name: Zimmerman
runners_data.note: Most interesting horse in the race on a pure form basis: won over 16f on soft just three days ago at Carlisle, which is almost the exact conditions replicated here; Tim Easterby sends him straight back quickly and the horse's hold-up style is authentic, but being mapped into midfield rather than its natural rear position is a structural disadvantage — the soft-ground stamina angle remains compelling despite the style-fit concern.
runners_data.comment: Zimmerman showed he retains ability with a win last time out, but three days is a quick turnaround and his inconsistency — two sixths in his last five starts — gives pause; he has run over today's trip and going, and 133 lb is no featherweight.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who has posted three thirds and a fourth from five soft-ground starts, showing he handles these conditions without winning on them; Jim Goldie's yard is active (5/40) and Shay Farmer takes the ride — the uncontested lead over 1m6f on soft is a significant tactical asset that elevates his chance above bare form figures.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below most of his rivals on our figures and ranked seventh of eight, Cascade Hall is hard to fancy despite that seventh last time out following two thirds beforehand; he has run over today's trip and going, and the win six starts back shows he can produce when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Easwrith Destiny
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old carrying the lowest weight (128lbs) in the field — the age and inexperience allowance gives David Menuisier's runner a significant pull at the weights; placed second on soft ground over 10f earlier in its short career and the prominent style should see it travel comfortably, though jumping from 10f to 14f is a stamina question that the soft ground will expose quickly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Easwrith Destiny faces a stiff ask here, though a second two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement for each-way hopes.

races.paceDynamic: Cascade Hall is the lone confirmed front-runner and will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset, setting a sustainable but controlling gallop over 1m6f on soft ground at Haydock. Dance Time and Easwrith Destiny will press forward from a prominent position, giving Cascade Hall company without truly threatening the lead, meaning the pace is genuine but not combustive. The soft going over this trip will stretch stamina reserves significantly, favouring horses who travel comfortably in the first half of the race rather than those who need to make up ground late. This race shape clearly favours front-running and prominent racing profiles — Cascade Hall's uncontested lead on soft ground is a powerful tactical advantage, and hold-up horses face an uphill task on this going over this distance. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Gentle Warrior, Expressionless, and Zimmerman are genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield positions on the map, but Cascade Hall and Dance Time are most likely to actually secure their natural positions at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cascade Hall Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cascade Hall jumps well and immediately controls the tempo, setting a measured but punishing pace on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall has a clear lead within the first furlong and dictates precisely from the front, grinding out the soft ground conditions to his advantage over 1m6f; prominent types who track closely will be best placed to capitalise if he tires late, but his recent soft-ground course form suggests he handles these conditions well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Cascade Hall's early lead is tracked closely and a prominent racer picks him off in the straight.
scenarios.body: Dance Time or Easwrith Destiny tracks the leader through the race and, aided by fresh legs and an apprentice with good tactical awareness, produces a well-timed challenge over the final two furlongs on this stamina-sapping ground; the soft going rewards a prominent runner who has conserved energy rather than chasing from too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves deceptively strong and the field strings out, enabling the most resolute stayer to grind through.
scenarios.body: The soft ground turns the race into a true stamina examination and a horse with proven soft-going form over this trip emerges from the pack late; Zimmerman's recent winning form on soft ground over 16f is directly relevant here, and despite being pushed into a midfield position on the map, his true hold-up style could extract late value if the leaders empty.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and closers get an unexpected late run on desperate ground.
scenarios.body: A strong early tempo set by Cascade Hall burns out the prominent runners, opening a late window for genuine hold-up types tracking from the rear; however, this scenario is materially discounted because Gentle Warrior, Expressionless, and Zimmerman are all redistributed horses racing out of their natural position, meaning true hold-up delivery is structurally compromised in this race shape.

watchPoints.text: Zimmerman won over 16f on soft just three days ago and returns to near-identical conditions — watch whether Tim Easterby's quick turnaround strategy is a bold strike or leaves the horse physically short, as his true hold-up style is compromised by being pushed into a midfield map position.

Cascade Hall's ability to control the tempo completely unchallenged is the defining tactical factor — if he jumps slowly or is pressured early by Dance Time, the entire race shape changes and prominent trackers rather than the leader himself will benefit.

Dance Time has only one soft-ground run in the last 15 starts — watch the going report for any deterioration, as a further softening surface could expose this horse's limited soft-ground experience at a critical point in the home straight.

Easwrith Destiny carries the lightest weight but jumps from 10f to 1m6f for the first time — a horse getting outpaced and stopping suddenly on soft ground could cause interference to hold-up horses coming from the rear, particularly Zimmerman and Gentle Warrior.

Yellow Card's form over 20f-22f on good ground is eye-catching but those trips are on a completely different speed and stamina profile to 1m6f on soft — watch whether Isobelle Chalmers attempts to use that stamina by tracking up early, which would represent a significant tactical shift in riding style.

races.name: Lee Thomas Christy Memorial Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Tattersalls £40,000 Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Etonnante
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field and a confirmed early-speed type for Karl Burke; her last two runs were on good ground at Goodwood, so soft conditions are an unknown, but the STYLE_FIT flag here is less concern than usual given she is mapping squarely into the role the race shape creates — lone leader.|

runners_data.name: Californian Angel
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's OR 120 filly carries the highest rating in the field and ran respectably in bigger company at Goodwood, but her natural instinct to race from the rear means she must produce a sustained finish into soft ground against a leader who will have banked energy; the redistribution to midfield overstates her forward position — she is a true closer who needs a strongly-run race to shine.|

runners_data.name: Marsala
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett sends a 23-day freshened filly who has experience at 7f at Sandown (soft/standard) and 6f at Goodwood, and that stamina profile could give her a late-run edge if soft conditions blunt Etonnante; she is a genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to have been genuine to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Novah
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's lightly-raced filly has one outing to her name — eighth of a big field over 6f on good at Haydock — and carries an explicit fade-in-finish flag that is especially damaging in a race where the leader is likely to be bowling along unchallenged; Faye McManoman will need to be creative to manufacture any winning chance.

races.paceDynamic: Etonnante is the sole confirmed front-runner in a four-runner field and, uncontested, will stride into an untroubled lead from the gates and set whatever tempo she chooses on soft ground at Haydock. With Californian Angel, Marsala, and Novah all hold-up types by profile, Etonnante faces no genuine pace rival, meaning the fractions will be dictated entirely on her terms — likely steady to modest given the soft going. This creates a race where the leader controls every variable: tempo, position, and the point at which rivals must commit. The tactical verdict is clear — this shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile that can dictate and be the hunter rather than the hunted, and Etonnante sits in exactly that role; note that the three hold-up fillies are true closers who will be working into a likely uncontested lead from the rear, reducing their margin for error considerably.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Etonnante Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Etonnante bowls into a soft, uncontested lead and sets a comfortable pace that her rivals can never close down in testing ground.
scenarios.body: Etonnante dictates the tempo throughout, and the soft going rewards those who travel smoothly rather than those asked to make up ground from off the pace; no rival has the natural early speed to challenge her leadership. The three hold-up fillies face the worst possible shape — chasing a leader who has banked energy reserves while they must expend energy overcoming ground and deficit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Trio Overrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and Etonnante ties up under the burden of soft ground, allowing closers to mow her down late.
scenarios.body: Soft conditions can expose a front-runner who has gone too fast early, and if Etonnante's fractions prove injudicious, Californian Angel and Marsala — both lightly raced two-year-olds with scope — could reel her in across the final furlong. This scenario demands near-perfect timing from jockeys on closers who may themselves have been stuck wider or racing at unfamiliar tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Marsala Picks Off Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Marsala, whose form over 7f at Sandown suggests stamina for soft ground over 6f, produces a sustained late run that the others cannot match.
scenarios.body: Marsala's trip profile and trainer Ralph Beckett's record with stayers suggests she may relish the slog of soft 6f more than her rivals who have only shown speed on good ground; she would need Etonnante to have set a genuinely testing pace. A clean passage from Hector Crouch and a strong gallop from the front would be required to create enough gaps for her to exploit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Novah Finds Late Form
scenarios.trigger: If Novah overcomes her noted tendency to fade in the finish and benefits from a true-run race that plays to raw ability over Etonnante's tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: Novah's single run record — a modest eighth on good ground at Haydock — provides minimal evidence of the improvement needed, and her fade-in-finish flag under soft conditions makes this the least likely outcome. Only a significantly underperforming field and a collapse across the board would bring her into contention.

watchPoints.text: Etonnante's soft-ground stamina is unproven — if she ties up inside the final furlong after controlling the race throughout, Californian Angel and Marsala have the class to capitalise rapidly.

Californian Angel is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield — David Probert must ensure she is not caught wide or forced to commit earlier than ideal, or her true closer's profile is fully compromised.

Novah's fade-in-finish flag combined with soft ground is a significant double concern — watch whether she is taken off her feet early in a race where even a gentle gallop may still prove too taxing for her given her sole outing profile.

With only four runners and a single front-runner, any first-fence jostling for the two or three position among Californian Angel, Marsala, and Novah could determine who secures the best stalking spot and who is trapped widest on the turn.

races.name: Oakmere Homes Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Milford
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Julie Camacho in visor; soft ground is fine on paper but recent form string (4-6092) is unimpressive and five similar-going runs have yielded zero wins and one place — watch for another effort that flatters to deceive.
runners_data.comment: Milford has run over today's trip and going and shaped with promise when second last time out, returning after 24 days in good order; yet to win in his last five starts, but drawn in stall one and top-rated here, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from 78 days off for Richard Hannon; has won on soft and finished second on soft before, and an uncontested lead here is a genuine asset — freshness is the key unknown after that layoff.
runners_data.comment: Wild Clary won two starts back and has placed twice more in recent starts, showing consistent form, but a 78-day absence and a trainer in a deep losing run give real cause for caution at 140 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Territorial Knight
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's prominent racer showed a soft-ground place on his card (2nd/6f/SOF) and Tom Eaves keeps the ride; trainer in strong form (4 wins from 37 in 14 days) and he is likely to press Wild Clary, giving him every chance if she tires.
runners_data.comment: Territorial Knight ran a solid second two starts back and returns on familiar distance and going terms after a 24-day break, with our rating of 88 suggesting he holds more than enough ability to threaten at the top of this field; the concern is he has been winless in his last five starts and must prove he can convert.

runners_data.name: Kodi Lion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Michael Appleby whose form figures on both soft and good have been very poor of late (9-9-5-13-9); Cieren Fallon takes over but six furlongs on soft looks like damage limitation rather than opportunity.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kodi Lion nevertheless catches the eye with distance and going experience and a rating of 89 that marks him as a genuine threat at the head of the rankings — the concern is that his recent finishes offer little encouragement he can translate that promise into a telling run here.

runners_data.name: Woven
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type with a pace-hood, trained by Michael Dods; has a soft-ground win in his past five and does handle conditions, but age and a modest recent string (0-4729) make winning hard to envisage even from a good position.
runners_data.comment: Woven shaped with real promise when a close second two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him every chance from stall three carrying 137 lb, though he remains winless in recent starts and that ninth last time out demands some forgiveness.

runners_data.name: Reciprocated
runners_data.note: Laura Pearson rides this David Loughnane 3-year-old who races prominently; form since a win has deteriorated quickly (5-3000) and three recent runs on soft have all produced finishing positions of 11th, 15th or worse — hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Reciprocated nonetheless has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and at 135 lb from stall five he remains competitive on a mark of 84, though consecutive unplaced efforts make improvement essential here.

runners_data.name: Never Just A Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for T J Kent who has only one placing from 15 runs on similar ground; six furlongs on soft is genuinely testing for him and Callum Rodriguez will need things to go perfectly, which they rarely do from the back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Never Just A Dream does at least bring distance experience and a fitness edge at 24 days, though carrying 133 lb from stall 11 and a largely unimpressive recent record — including two unplaced efforts in his last four — leave him with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Coachello
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with a pace-hood, trained by Mark Loughnane; has run exclusively on soft/standard of late without threatening, and an eight-race winless run makes this a difficult profile to back at any price.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Coachello at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and 13 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, an eighth last time out and carrying 133 lb from stall 12 make it hard to see him forcing his way into the argument.

runners_data.name: Cargin Bhui
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last two wins came on standard ground at distances of 6-7f; mapped to midfield here because so many closers cannot all sit at the rear — this forced positional compromise, combined with 145 days off, dilutes what is otherwise a horse with winning form.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 145 days makes Cargin Bhui difficult to trust on his return, and our figures rank him 12th of 14 in the field; however, he has experience over today's trip and going, and his two wins in his last six starts show he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's seven-year-old is a true hold-up horse who has run exclusively on good ground in his last five, all at this course and distance; he is nudged into a midfield position on the map because the field is saturated with hold-up types, and his soft-ground profile is genuinely unproven.
runners_data.comment: Grant Wood has run over today's trip and going, and a fourth two starts back offers mild encouragement, but he has been winless in recent starts and his ranking of tenth of fourteen leaves him with plenty to find on a mark of 77.

runners_data.name: Ran Amok
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 4-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has soft-ground form of real quality (2nd/6f/SOF, 5th, 7th, 10th); David Probert rides and his prominent style suits this scenario well — the 76-day absence is the only concern.
runners_data.comment: Ran Amok has been winless in his last five starts and, ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has run over today's trip and going before and shaped with some promise when third last time out, 76 days ago.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse flagged as a fader in the finish, with headgear noted; his best soft-ground form is thin (1W from 15 runs on sim going) and being pushed into midfield by field congestion removes the one thing that made his style viable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lord Bertie nonetheless steps up with an 8 lb pull between his official mark and our rating, and has experience over today's trip and conditions; the concern is a string of unplaced efforts that suggests he needs things to drop right from stall 13 off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Tip Foster
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old for David & Nicola Barron with only two runs showing a win and a placed effort, both with promise; returning after 91 days but the soft-ground placed run (3rd/6f/SOF) gives encouragement and Joanna Mason's claim could be meaningful if this improves.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Tip Foster faces a stiff ask, though he won last time out and has run over today's trip, with stall two his draw; the 91-day absence is another question mark against him.

runners_data.name: Trust Amy
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who is nudged into midfield on the map due to field congestion among closers; has soft-ground form (3rd/6f/SOF in recent history) and Gina Mangan rides, but OR 69 is the lowest in the field and the weight-for-age 3-year-old profile makes winning against older rivals a big ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes of ninth and two eighths among them, Trust Amy is hard to fancy from stall seven carrying 120 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and the third two starts back offers a crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Clary is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival prepared to push her hard for the early lead, she should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground over six furlongs at Haydock. Territorial Knight, Kodi Lion, Reciprocated, and Ran Amok will press from prominent positions but none is a natural front-runner seeking to take on Wild Clary directly, meaning the early pace is unlikely to be truly brutal. The soft going at Haydock tends to stretch fields and reward horses who travel economically close to the pace rather than those making up ground from far back — a truly run, even-tempo race on this surface typically sees closers beaten for toe at the death, not rewarded. This race shape therefore favours prominent racers who can track Wild Clary within a length or two and have the soft-ground stamina to pick her off in the final furlong; pure hold-up horses face a compounded disadvantage because several of them — Grant Wood, Cargin Bhui, Lord Bertie, and Trust Amy — are true hold-up types who will be unable to secure their natural rear position with so many off-the-pace horses in the same field, forcing them to race closer than ideal without the tactical benefit of doing so.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominence Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Clary dictates a fair but sustainable gallop and prominent chasers pick her off in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Wild Clary sets a measured tempo on soft ground, and a horse travelling smoothly just behind her has the ideal run — soft Haydock six furlongs rewards exactly this profile, as the ground saps finishing kicks from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Wild Clary Runs Right Through
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Clary is fully fresh after 78 days off, softens the field's finishing speed, and simply outstays everyone from the front.
scenarios.body: After a break, Richard Hannon's mare bounces back with a confidence-building lead on ground she has won on before, and no rival has the boot to close on a true front-runner who has controlled every second of the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds, Stayer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and soft conditions extract maximum stamina, elevating a horse with proven soft-ground resolution.
scenarios.body: A notch more tempo from Territorial Knight or Reciprocated pressing Wild Clary turns the race into a stamina test, and a horse whose form figures on soft ground carry most weight comes home best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly collapses late and a closer threads a clear run through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because the genuine hold-up horses — Grant Wood, Cargin Bhui, Lord Bertie — are forced out of their natural rear position and gain none of the positional advantage that makes late runs work; soft ground further blunts their finishing speed.

watchPoints.text: Wild Clary sets off uncontested from the front — if she bowls along at a controlled tempo on soft ground, she may simply never be headed; watch whether Territorial Knight or Reciprocated have the courage to push early and force a true gallop.

Grant Wood, Cargin Bhui, Lord Bertie, and Trust Amy are all genuine hold-up horses forced into a midfield role by field congestion — if any of them drifts back to their natural position, they will face a near-impossible task making up ground on soft ground over six furlongs.
Ran Amok returns after 76 days off for Hugo Palmer — if that absence has sharpened rather than blunted him, his soft-ground form makes him a live danger, but fitness on reappearance is unverified.

Tip Foster has run only twice but both runs showed promise including a soft-ground placing — with Joanna Mason's 7lb claim, this lightly raced 3-year-old could outrun a big price if the race tempo suits prominent runners.

Soft going at Haydock can catch horses out for stamina in the final furlong — monitor early sectionals to judge whether Wild Clary is truly conserving or if the field will compress sharply in the closing stages.

races.name: Aesterius At Bearstone Stud Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Changeofmind
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course, distance and going combination last time out (1/5f/SOF); Connor Wheatley's hold-up ride suits this pace scenario well and the 15-day turnaround is straightforward for a horse in form — the race shape here is tailor-made.
runners_data.comment: Changeofmind ran well to finish second last time out and has experience over today's trip and conditions, but his three starts before that produced a sixth, seventh and eighth, suggesting inconsistency tempers his claims despite carrying a manageable 140 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Secret Mistral
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's front-runner won over 5f Good last time and races fresh off just 9 days; the risk is that Jer Batt and Creative Queen will fight for the lead alongside her, making an uncontested front-running display unlikely — soft ground is unproven (1 run).
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom-two on our figures and carrying a hefty 139 lb from stall ten, Secret Mistral is hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and the fact she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who holds up but all five recent runs have come on Good ground at 5f; the step into Soft going is the significant unknown for this Michael Dods runner and his form line doesn't inspire confidence at present.
runners_data.comment: Mighty Magnus showed his quality with a win five starts back and was third three starts back, giving him strong recent form credentials at this level; the concern is that he has been unplaced on his latest start and must prove he bounces back from that run off 138 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez rides a horse with strong placed form (three 3rds in four recent runs) but Jer Batt's soft-ground record is poor (7th/5f/SOF, 7th/5f/HEA) and the stable's T14 of 0/10 adds cold-yard concern — wants to lead but will face fierce early competition.
runners_data.comment: Jer Batt shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back and third three starts back, and our rating of 87 ranks him the pick of this field; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and his last run ended in a fourth, suggesting the winning moment may still be coming.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's hold-up five-year-old has won over 5f Good and placed on Soft; with a T14 of 0/23 the stable is out of form, but William Pyle's ride through a fast pace suits the style and the going record is acceptable.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Accrual has run over today's trip and going and returns on a workable 21-day break, but his trainer is winless from 23 runners in the past fortnight, which is a notable headwind under 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Lipsink
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing nine-year-old who has won twice at 5-6f on Soft and hit the frame repeatedly in similar conditions; Alistair Rawlinson keeps him competitive, the 6-day turnaround shows fitness, and he maps well just behind the likely lead battle.
runners_data.comment: Lipsink has shown ability in his last five starts, with a second last time out and a win five starts back, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures he faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going and returns on a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's seven-year-old has strong placed form on Soft (2/6f/SOF, 2/5f/SOF) and two wins in this going band; cheekpieces noted, Shay Farmer's 5lb claim is an asset, and racing prominently he could exploit any collapse in the pace-setters.

runners_data.name: Spoof
runners_data.note: An eleven-year-old veteran with 11 runs in Soft and three wins in this going; last won off 5f/SOF and the form is live if fresh after 87 days — the hold-up style suits the pace dynamic but fitness after nearly three months is the only question.
runners_data.comment: Spoof won two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, giving him solid claims here; drawn in stall two and carrying 135 lb, he arrives fresh on an 87-day break but shaped well enough to demand respect.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has done his work on Good ground (all five recent runs); a genuine hold-up type whose natural position will be compromised by this field's pace configuration — forced forward out of role and without soft-ground evidence, his chance is materially discounted.
runners_data.comment: Boston Dan has run over today's trip and going, and at a rating of 84 he shapes as a genuine danger from stall five, returning on a sharp 16-day turnaround; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's five-year-old holds no wins or places in recent soft-ground history and all recent form is on Good; likely to race prominently but the going evidence is thin and the stable's T14 of 3/16 is modest — needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: American Bay arrives here 22 days fresh, has run over today's trip, and shaped with promise when second four starts back, but seven in his most recent outing and winless in his last six starts suggest he faces a stiff task from stall 12 off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old won over 6f Soft and has a headgear flag (blinkers) to sharpen focus; she will attempt to lead but with two other confirmed front-runners she faces a genuine pace battle — if forced to concede the lead she may find this race shape too messy.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Creative Queen faces a stiff ask, though she arrives on the back of a placed effort last time out and has experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Moonstone Boy
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's five-year-old returns after 147 days off — a significant absence — and while headgear (cheekpieces) is flagged, all recent form is on faster ground; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position will be compressed by others, and the layoff plus going switch make this a difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 147 days, Moonstone Boy has plenty to prove stepping back in, and a ranking of 11th of 12 on our figures makes him very hard to fancy, despite having run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Mistral, Jer Batt, and Creative Queen are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead from the off, virtually guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop over this 5f on Soft ground — with three horses all wanting to be on the pace, none of them will get an easy, uncontested lead. The resulting fast early sectionals will be gruelling in soft conditions, stretching the race out and burning off those who cannot travel economically behind a hot pace. Hold-up horses such as Changeofmind, Accrual, and Spoof — who love this ground — are set to be the chief beneficiaries, able to conserve energy through the early stages and pick up beaten rivals in the final furlong. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the map can accommodate: Boston Dan and Moonstone Boy are genuine come-from-behind horses who will likely find themselves shuffled forward out of their natural position due to the race shape, so their true hold-up profiles should be discounted accordingly. This race shape squarely favours hold-up horses with proven soft-ground credentials who can close powerfully through a tired field in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Mistral, Jer Batt, and Creative Queen set a genuinely strong gallop that burns each other out on the Soft surface.
scenarios.body: The three pace-setters cut each other's throats through the first half of the race, leaving the field strung out and tired; proven soft-ground hold-up performers charging through late will find the most to gain.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners edges clear early but the pace is strong enough to set it up for a prominent racer sitting just behind the lead.
scenarios.body: A horse in the second or third position avoids the worst of the early battle while still travelling close enough to pounce at the two-furlong pole; the Soft going tests stamina but a prominent runner with soft-ground form can sustain the effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Horse Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most plausibly Creative Queen or Secret Mistral — steals a march and secures a clear, unchallenged lead before the others can react.
scenarios.body: A single pace-setter who controls the fractions on their own terms can dictate a more measured gallop and conserve enough energy to hold on up the soft 5f straight; Haydock's 5f is undemanding in terms of turns but the ground will still test any leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Miss The Boat
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but the ground is slow enough that the finishing kick is compressed and the race is won by a prominent type rather than a true hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: Soft ground can occasionally blunt the late run of closers if they cannot find a clear path through a tightly grouped field in the straight; a prominent horse with proven soft-ground form who avoids trouble in running benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Watch the early exchanges between Secret Mistral, Jer Batt, and Creative Queen — if all three fight for the lead simultaneously, the resulting pace could be extreme even by soft-ground standards, collapsing the winning time and making hold-up horses almost essential.
Spoof's 87-day absence is the key fitness flag — he has three soft-ground wins and a style that suits perfectly, but if he needs the run he will fail to pick up at the crucial moment in the straight.

Boston Dan and Moonstone Boy are both true hold-up horses who will struggle to find their natural position behind this pace; if either is forced to race more prominently than usual, form-based expectations should be heavily discounted.

Lipsink's freshness (6-day turnaround) and Parisiac's cheekpieces are both live tactical upgrades — either could be sharper than market implies if the pace-setters collapse as expected in the closing stages.
Changeofmind's winning soft-ground course-and-distance form is the standout piece of evidence in this field — monitor market moves on this runner as it profiles ideally for the dominant scenario.

races.name: Arete Foundation Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Folkene
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Roger Fell with Joanna Mason in the saddle; her soft-going form reads poorly (6th of 7f/SOF in recent history, 0 wins from 8 comparable-going starts), and she'll be hunting cover from the back of midfield in a race likely to be too strong a pace for a late run to materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Folkene shaped with promise when fourth last time out and again three starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going she rates a solid each-way danger from stall seven; the risk is that she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an immediate concern on Soft ground with 12 runners, and his recent form at 6f on soft and standard is not encouraging; a hold-up type who has to find a significantly better performance than recent finishes suggest.|

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's three-year-old has solid 7f form on Good going (1st and multiple placings), is ridden by a 5lb claimer which reduces the weight burden meaningfully, and his prominent style suits this shape well — the key question is whether he can reproduce that Good-ground form on today's Soft.|
runners_data.comment: Homestrait won three starts back and has placed twice more in recent starts, showing she has the profile to go close here, and her experience over today's trip and going adds substance to her claims; the worry is a trainer operating at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Magic Music
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won at 7f on Good and has consistently competed at this trip; Steph Hollinshead's yard has run just once in 14 days (1/4), and Luke Catton's 3lb claim helps at the weights — well-positioned in the market of running styles for this pace-hot scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Magic Music won three starts back but has posted a fifth and a sixth since, suggesting she may be over that peak; she has run over today's trip and comes into this fresh on 28 days off, though 136 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Dream Illusion
runners_data.note: David Probert takes the ride on this hold-up type who has Soft-adjacent placed form (2nd on Standard, 2nd on Good) at 7f; 18 days since last run keeps her fresh, and she is one of the more credible finishers if the leaders genuinely collapse in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Dream Illusion shapes as a consistent, if winless, contender — second last time out and fourth three starts back suggest she finds a way into the frame, though that eighth two starts back is a concern, and 136 lb from stall eight adds further pressure.

runners_data.name: Clementines Star
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners and perhaps the most tractable of the trio based on her 3-2-1-3 form sequence; William Carver rides for the Kubler yard who have not run in the past 14 days, and she has shown the ability to make the running and win at 7f on Good — whether that translates to Soft is the outstanding doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Clementines Star arrives here in the form of her life, placed last time out and a winner two starts back, and she has run over today's trip before. Carrying 135 lb from stall five, her overall profile makes her our pick in this field.

runners_data.name: Toralou
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old has two placed efforts on Soft in her recent history and genuine hold-up tendencies; the redistribution note reflects the reality that with three true front-runners already present, she is shown in midfield but will likely drop back towards her natural position — her STYLE_FIT of 0.91 cautions against expecting her to replicate form from a compromised berth.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Toralou does at least show a second three starts back to suggest she retains some ability, though sixth and seventh-place finishes since then are a concern; she has run over today's trip and returns after 24 days, but has plenty to find at a rating of 65.

runners_data.name: Imelda
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's three-year-old is a confirmed pace-setter whose recent 2-3-3-4 form at 7f includes Soft and Standard placed efforts; 56 days off the track is a significant concern on soft ground in a competitive handicap, and she may find one or both of her fellow front-runners too strong if a true battle breaks out from the gates.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Imelda is hard to fancy on these terms, though she has run over today's trip and her recent placings show she is no stranger to competing — she just needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's five-year-old is the most battle-hardened of the three front-runners with a win over 8f on Good and solid recent activity (ran 7 days ago); T14 strike of 4/23 suggests a yard in decent form, but his best form has come over a mile on Good — dropping to 7f on Soft with early rivals to fight is a test of his stamina and willingness to race wide open.|
runners_data.comment: Cypriot Diaspora arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, while our rating of 72 marks her out as a serious threat from stall two; the main concern is whether she can reproduce that form off a seven-day turnaround carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's three-year-old won over 8f on Soft (his only soft-ground start) which is a notable positive on today's surface, and he has the staying profile to grind out a result if the race turns truly gruelling; he races from the hold-up position and will need the pace to be savage to make his finishing kick count over 7f.|
runners_data.comment: Gelato won two starts back but has finished fifth and struggled in the three starts either side of that success, and with her trainer striking at just five per cent in the past fortnight, she makes little appeal despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in excellent form (T14: 10/87) and David Allan knows the horse, but this is a genuine hold-up horse facing the challenge of racing in a midfield position it doesn't naturally occupy — the blinkers (hg:b) may sharpen early focus, but its soft-ground record of one placing from 14 comparable starts tempers enthusiasm.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back suggests she retains some ability, but five starts without a win and a fifth last time out paint a mixed picture; has run over today's trip and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround from stall 11 carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has five consecutive fifth-place finishes which tells a story of consistency without acceleration; a natural hold-up runner shown in midfield due to redistribution, it has raced on Soft before without threatening (5th/8f/SOF), and its STYLE_FIT flag suggests expecting a reproduction of its true running pattern to be optimistic in this tactical scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of fourth and fifth-place finishes painting a consistent but frustrating picture, Light The Night Up is hard to fancy from stall ten off 127 lb, though she has run over today's trip and returns on a sharp 11-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Imelda, Clementines Star, and Cypriot Diaspora are all confirmed front-runners, and with three genuine pace horses in a 12-runner field over 7f on Soft ground, an honest, stamina-sapping gallop is virtually guaranteed from the outset. These three will fight for early supremacy, ensuring no false economy in the early fractions, and the compounding effect of Soft going will make this a genuine test of resolution and staying power in the final two furlongs. Horses who can track the pace efficiently from a prominent or mid-pack position — saving energy while remaining close enough to strike — will be best placed, as the leaders burn each other off and the race falls apart in the home straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race map can accommodate: Toralou, Only Dream Big, and Light The Night Up are genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield, with Toralou and Light The Night Up most likely to secure that position if they choose it, though true wait-and-pounce tactics over 7f in deep ground are high-risk from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours horses who race prominently but just off the leading trio — the patient traveller who doesn't burn fuel early yet stays in range to pounce as the front runners tie up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out and the race becomes a war of attrition in the last two furlongs on Soft ground.
scenarios.body: Imelda, Clementines Star, and Cypriot Diaspora push hard from the jump, and the relentless pace on Soft turf drains them all before the finish; a prominent horse who settles just behind the speed in the first two furlongs finds a clear path as the leaders capitulate. Homestrait and Magic Music, positioned prominently with strong 7f form on similar ground, are ideally placed to grind past the tiring leaders in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Clementines Star — establishes a clear lead and controls the tempo without burning excessive energy.
scenarios.body: Should the other two early types be content to slot in behind rather than fight for every inch, Clementines Star's course-and-distance profile and recent winning run at this trip could allow her to control fractions and steal a march on the field. On Soft going, a horse who leads without duress can maintain a rhythm that suits, and her handlers' lighter strike-rate (T14:0/6) suggests she arrives fresh and perhaps undercooked for rivals to assess.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the gruelling Soft conditions turn the race into a thorough stamina test and the winner comes from slightly further back having been ridden more conservatively.
scenarios.body: A truly testing surface over 7f can occasionally reward a horse who is dropped in mid-pack and delivered with one sustained run from two furlongs out, particularly if all the prominent types are compromised by earlier energy expenditure. Dream Illusion, who has shown a liking for this trip and has Soft-ground placed form, and Gelato, a winner on Soft over a mile, could both benefit if the leaders set an extreme early pace that fully unravels the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners implode catastrophically and the race opens up dramatically for true hold-up horses in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This outcome depends on Toralou, Only Dream Big, or Light The Night Up — all genuinely hold-up types — overcoming the significant challenge of finding clear daylight through a tiring field in a race they are unlikely to contest from their natural position given the crowded rear. The [REDISTRIBUTED] flags on all three reduce this scenario's credibility materially, as none are likely to be in their preferred spot, making a late sweep from the back a low-probability outcome however strong the pace becomes.

watchPoints.text: Imelda, Clementines Star, and Cypriot Diaspora — watch for a heated early battle for the lead; if all three push hard from the gates, the pace could be suicidal on Soft ground and any of them could stop to nothing in the final furlong, opening the race wide for Homestrait or Magic Music to swoop.

Imelda — 56 days off the track is a material concern for a front-runner on Soft ground; watch her in the preliminaries and early strides for any signs that the layoff has left her short of peak fitness, which could cause her to drop away sharply after leading early.

Pickersgill — ran just two days ago and is asked to back up quickly on Soft going; jockey Paul Mulrennan will likely conserve energy early but the quick turnaround must be flagged as a fitness and freshness risk.

Toralou, Only Dream Big, Light The Night Up — all three are genuinely hold-up horses displaced to midfield on the race map; watch to see if any of them drop back to their natural position from the outset, which would confirm the redistribution and mean the midfield is thinner than it appears, potentially opening a cleaner passage for a prominent runner to dominate.

Gelato — his sole win came on Soft going over further (8f), making him the standout candidate if today's conditions produce a truly extreme stamina test; watch whether Finley Marsh settles him patiently in the early stages, as that will signal an intent to make his ground-specific finishing run count over the shorter 7f trip.

races.name: Betfair Supports Racing Welfare Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hamadhan
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trained by Jennie Candlish, returning after 97 days off; form on similar soft ground is thin (0W0P in 7 sim-going runs) and a trip of 1m3½f represents an unknown quantity on today's going — needs the race to be run to suit closers.
runners_data.comment: Hamadhan shaped with promise when third last time out and, rated 85 by us against an official mark of 75, he looks a serious threat from stall 8 carrying 142 lb, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour; the main risk is a 97-day absence leaving him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Flash Bardot
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with genuine soft-ground credentials (2P from 10 sim-going runs), handles big fields, but a 113-day absence and an age-profile that suits longer trips than today's 1m3½f are mild reservations; Cieren Fallon's booking is the positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Flash Bardot arrives carrying 141 lb from stall seven on a mark of 74, and her experience over today's trip and going stands her in good stead, with our rating of 87 making her the pick of 13; winless in her last five starts and 113 days since her most recent outing are the obvious reservations.

runners_data.name: Lightning Tiger
runners_data.note: Consistent but frustrating sort who keeps posting fours; the headgear change (hood added) signals connections searching for a spark, and Charlie Fellowes sends one runner in 14 days which is a workmanlike but not burning confidence signal — soft ground at Haydock is genuinely within his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Lightning Tiger has been a model of consistency, finishing fourth in four of his last five starts, and with experience over today's trip and conditions, he arrives with solid claims at a mark of 73; the concern is that eighth last time out raises questions about his current form.

runners_data.name: Yokohama
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on soft ground (sole win in sim-going) so the trip and conditions are fair, but this is a true hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear; in a race with minimal pace, Conor Whiteley (5) will find it very hard to get Yokohama into a winning position from where the map places him.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back and shaped with credit when third two starts back, and Yokohama has experience of both today's trip and going; the primary concern is a trainer badly out of form at 1/20 over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Tortured Soul
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll fires 7/55 over 14 days suggesting an in-form string; Molly Gunn (5) takes the ride and the recent form is consistent with placings — but all five visible runs are on Standard, never soft, so today's ground is an untested variable for a horse whose real home is deep in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but no stranger to the places, Tortured Soul brings distance and going experience to the table from draw six carrying 139 lb, though 123 days off the track and a rating of 76 ranking him seventh of thirteen suggest a midfield pitch is the realistic expectation.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: The name is ironic — this is actually a confirmed hold-up horse, displaced further into midfield today by sheer numbers; Sam England sends runners fit (28-day turnaround, headgear worn), but soft ground form on the flat is absent and longer trips of 14-17f suggest today's 1m3½f could be on the short side.
runners_data.comment: Third on two of his last three starts suggests consistent placing ability, but a sixth last time out clouds his claims; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 136 lb from stall five, and his recent consistency may be offset by that latest disappointing effort.

runners_data.name: Blue Wonder
runners_data.note: Won on soft ground over 10f (1W1P from 10 sim-going runs) so conditions suit, and Clifford Lee is a capable pilot; but this is a genuine hold-up horse crammed into midfield by the field's back-heavy shape — with a pedestrian pace expected, Lee will struggle to find a racing position that delivers Blue Wonder's best.
runners_data.comment: Blue Wonder showed she can win at this level when landing the spoils two starts back, yet a fifth last time out — after 83 days off — suggests she returns needing this run, and 135 lb is no gimme from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Star Time
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and therefore controls the tempo entirely; Alan King has one winner from nine over 14 days (not booming), and Harry Vigors (5) is a 5lb claimer who must judge the pace on soft ground — with no rivals to press, the danger is going too slow and being swamped.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Star Time faces a stiff ask ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, and his 134 lb burden from stall 13 does nothing to ease that task; third last time out at least hints at residual ability, and he does have experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by Ralph Beckett, a trainer renowned for improving fillies over middle distances; limited form (three runs, all Standard or Good), so soft ground and 1m3½f are genuinely unknown quantities — the upside is there but the evidence base is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Marianita faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns after a 39-day break that may have freshened her up.

runners_data.name: Naturalia
runners_data.note: The only other genuine prominent-type in the field alongside Star Time; five recent runs show a 1W3P record in sim-going conditions, including a win on soft over 10f — stepping to 1m3½f on Haydock soft could be the making of her if she can sit just off Star Time without fighting for position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Naturalia faces a stiff ask against this field, yet she arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, offering at least some positives to cling to.

runners_data.name: Lesrico
runners_data.note: Soft-ground winner (1W3P from 13 sim-going runs) and headgear worn (hood) — the form over 10f on soft is real; a hold-up horse in nature, and the redistribution into midfield compounds the tactical problem, but if the race does string out on testing ground this one can stay on.

runners_data.name: Green Falcon
runners_data.note: David Menuisier has gone 0/16 in 14 days which is a cold run for a usually shrewd handler; the horse ran 13th over 12f on Good last time, and while earlier form at shorter trips on softer going was more encouraging, today's trip could stretch him — hold-up style is ill-suited to the anticipated race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well down on our figures, Green Falcon faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and drops to stall three carrying 131 lb, but an unplaced effort last time out after 41 days away makes it hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Michael Bell sends this three-year-old in solid form (1W from last 6, including a win over 8f on Good), and Ryan Kavanagh (3) claims 3lbs; but all the winning form is over 8f on Good or Standard — 1m3½f on soft at Haydock is a sharp step into the unknown for a horse whose natural style is from hold-up.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and fifth two starts back, Ziggy's Avenger has had a quiet spell of 39 days since his last outing, though he brings distance and going experience to the table; a win three starts back shows he can find the line, but his rating of 76 suggests he faces a stiff ask from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Star Time is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Naturalia as a genuine prominent-type companion, faces no serious early pressure — on soft ground at Haydock over 1m3½f this creates a truly dawdling gallop that could easily become a sprint-test from the home turn. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses (Yokohama, Tortured Soul, Made All, Blue Wonder, Lesrico, Green Falcon, Ziggy's Avenger), but the map overstates how many can genuinely settle at the rear — several of those are redistributed types who will crowd the midfield rather than form a true staying group at the back. With soft ground stretching stamina and a modest pace, the premium is on horses that can travel prominently without fighting for position, as late closers will need an injection of pace that this field shape is unlikely to generate. **Tactical verdict: the race shape strongly favours prominent-travelling horses who can dictate or sit just off Star Time's shoulder, with true hold-up types dependent on a pace injection that will probably never materialise.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Star Time bowls along at a steady clip and Naturalia sits tight behind, the race becomes a stamina-sapping procession on soft ground that rewards horses racing in the first four.
scenarios.body: Star Time sets a comfortable tempo with Naturalia tracking, and the absence of pressure means the front two control the entire shape through the home turn; closers have too much ground to make up on a soft surface without a fierce gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground takes a significant toll on the pace-setters in the final quarter-mile, stoic gallopers from the central pack grind past a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: The steady early fractions mean even midfield runners have been held up sufficiently to deliver a late effort, but the key is soft-ground stamina rather than a turn of foot; horses proven in this going and over this trip are the ones who capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Star Time is allowed to stride into the race unchallenged from the outset and the ground is testing enough to stop the closers from accelerating.
scenarios.body: Star Time dictates a tempo entirely of his own choosing, produces a perfect energy conservation run, and simply outstays a field that can never get on terms; soft ground ironically suits the front-runner if no rival forces a fast early pace to drain its reserves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Flourish From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and creating genuine space for true hold-up horses to unleash a finish.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a combination of factors — a jockey kicking for home earlier than expected and enough of a test to crack the prominent horses — but the redistributed hold-up types would need to race authentically from off the pace, which the race shape is unlikely to allow.

watchPoints.text: Star Time and Naturalia — if these two settle into any kind of rhythm together through the first mile, the rest of the field may never see daylight on soft ground; watch the early pace from the front to determine whether this becomes a true test or a sprint disguised as a staying race.

Yokohama and Blue Wonder are genuine hold-up horses wearing the label of midfield runners today — if they drift back to their natural position at the rear, they are racing into a graveyard given the lack of pace; watch where Whiteley and Lee actually sit in the first two furlongs.

Lesrico carries headgear and is proven on soft but must somehow overcome an unfavourable race shape — watch whether Ben Ffrench Davis attempts to push forward early against the horse's hold-up instincts to compensate.

Flash Bardot returns after 113 days and is bred and proven for soft ground over longer trips — watch whether Cieren Fallon targets a wide, prominent berth to mitigate the hold-up disadvantage given the anticipated modest pace.

Marianita for Ralph Beckett is unexposed on soft ground and could outrun her odds if conditions bring out previously unseen stamina — watch for any market support late in the day as a leading trainer's dark horse.
